verdicts: # §90.2.7 review — pharm notes cards (10 files) and places

**Method note (disclosure):** I ran only reads plus the brief's read-only helper (`spec.mjs check|aliases|suggest` on all 10 specs), and read the outlines, specs, plan rules (90 §90.2.6, §90.2.7, §90.3.1; 20 §20.6–20.8), the signed `ui-design/site-data.js` REF_TABS, `content/places/reftabs.json`, and her PANCE guide tables. No tests/lint/build were run. One deviation: to scan her PANCE guide's table rows for the home.pance check I briefly wrote a scan script (`scratch/emil/_scan_pance.mjs`), ran it once, and deleted it. Nothing else was written.
## FINDINGS
**F1 — behavioral-health: her three dosing tables and the SAMHSA note are all filed inside the "Alternative therapies" card.**
- File: `spec-behavioral-health-med-list-and-los-6.json`; part `anxalt @ b_1WYSXR3Q7J:106`.

- The Anxiety prose block ends at node 106; the next part starts at `b_8BED7D68MC:2`. In between sit, in file order: table `b_V8K2X17DM6` (benzodiazepine dosing — alprazolam, oxazepam, temazepam, midazolam, estazolam, triazolam, clonazepam, diazepam, flurazepam, lorazepam, chlordiazepoxide), empty prose `b_G2TEPGC4BY`, table `b_ETHVY5Z83X` (barbiturate dosing — phenobarbital, amobarbital, butabarbital, secobarbital, pentobarbital), prose `b_81AB4ZSAP8` (SAMHSA TIP 45 potency/withdrawal note, phenobarbital 30 mg unit), and table `b_MKGKA9C1TT` (buspirone, hydroxyzine, propranolol, atenolol, prazosin, clonidine dosing). All of it currently renders inside the card titled "Alternative therapies- do not need to know specific names".
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 cut points + 20 §20.6 (a card's slices are shown in file order; nothing mislabeled); the file's own content puts these tables with their drug classes.

- Correction: add parts so each table joins its class — `b_V8K2X17DM6:0 → card benzo`, `b_ETHVY5Z83X:0 → card barb`, `b_81AB4ZSAP8:0 → card barb`, `b_MKGKA9C1TT:0 → card otheranx` (its first rows are buspirone/hydroxyzine; note it also holds anxap drugs — one card per part forces the choice; `anxap` is the alternative). Coverage stays exact and ordered.
**F2 — GU: home.pance = reproductive-system for the ED/testosterone cards contradicts the blueprint and her PANCE guide.**
- File: `spec-gu-and-hematopoietic-drugs-med-lists-and-los.json`; cards `pde5ed`, `injvaso`, `testosterone`, `alprostadil` (`home: {pance: "reproductive-system"}`).

- Evidence: the NCCPA PANCE content blueprint (nccpa.net, effective Jan 2025) lists **Erectile dysfunction under Genitourinary System → "Penile disorders"** (GU 4%); the Reproductive System section (7%) contains no ED topic (pregnancy, menstrual, menopause, contraception, infertility, breast, uterine/vaginal/ovarian…). Her PANCE guide agrees on the teaching side: `content/guides/pance/endocrine-system/blocks/b_V8DRW4GVYG.json` holds the **Hypogonadism (⇣testosterone)** condition row, and the GU system holds the erectile/sildenafil mentions — `reproductive-system/` contains **zero** mentions of "erectile".
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 (`home.pance` = the PANCE system the card is taught under); brief item 8 asks each assignment be checked against the NCCPA grouping and her PANCE guide.

- Correction: `pde5ed`, `injvaso`, `alprostadil` → `renal-system-gu-system`. `testosterone` → `renal-system-gu-system` (keeps the ED group together; ED section is one topic in her file) or `endocrine-system` (where her PANCE guide actually teaches hypogonadism) — if the curator prefers the latter, take it to the Leader as a two-position item per §90.2.7.
**F3 — epilepsy: the GABA card's own drugs have no aliases, and they exist nowhere else in the file.**
- File: `spec-epilepsy-and-neurodegen-dz-med-list.json`; card `gaba` (part `@ b_M1BNJ7S2HM:82`), `aliases: []`.

- Card text (nodes 87–88): "Class members: BZDs - phenobarbital - valproic acid; also **tiagabine (Gabatril)** / **vigabatrin (Sabril)** - cenobamate…". Tiagabine and vigabatrin appear in no other card, so with no aliases the card can never attach and these two drugs have no card anywhere.
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 (aliases = every generic drug name in the card's text).

- Correction: add `tiagabine`, `vigabatrin`. (BZDs/phenobarbital/valproic acid/cenobamate on the same line are cross-references to their own cards — omitting those is consistent with convention 7 and fine.)
**F4 — GU: injvaso card omits the agents its own Administration list names.**
- File: `spec-gu-and-hematopoietic-drugs-med-lists-and-los.json`; card `injvaso`, `aliases: ["Injected vasodilators"]`.
- Card text (nodes 171–174): "Papaverine / Phentolamine / Bimix = papaverine + phentolamine / Trimix = … + alprostadil".
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 aliases.

- Correction: add `papaverine`, `phentolamine` (they have no card of their own). `alprostadil` optional — it has its own card; adding it would attach injvaso to alprostadil rows via trimix, which is accurate.
**F5 — GU: anticholbph card has zero aliases but its text names the drugs it recommends.**
- File: same spec; card `anticholbph` (`@ b_FQD1MDT10G:90`), `aliases: []`.
- Card text node 92: "Best: **tolterodine** ER + **tamsulosin** (Sx benefit)" — a clinical-use recommendation, not an interaction/algorithm step.
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 aliases.
- Correction: add `tolterodine` and `tamsulosin` (both are generics in the card's text; tamsulosin is already aliased on the a1 card, so the duplicate attachment is intended per 40 §40.4).
**F6 — behavioral-health: anxap card omits atenolol.**
- File: `spec-behavioral-health-med-list-and-los-6.json`; card `anxap`.
- Card text node 89: "β-blockers- **propranolol, atenolol**" (and the dosing table, per F1, rows for both). propranolol is aliased; atenolol is not.
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 aliases. Correction: add `atenolol`.
**F7 — GI: opioidconst heading names Naloxegol; alias missing.**
- File: `spec-gi-los-and-med-list-1.json`; card `opioidconst` (`@ b_TRHT1QX52V:599`), aliases `methylnaltrexone, naldemedine` only.
- Her heading: "Opioid Constipation: Methylnaltrexone (Relistor), Naldemedine (Symproic), **Naloxegol (Movantik)**".
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 aliases (generic names in the card's own text, heading included). Correction: add `naloxegol`.
**F8 — typo-only aliases will silently fail to match tables (verbatim whole-word matching).**

- Three cards carry her misspelling but not the correct generic spelling, unlike the correct handling elsewhere (cardio-1-1 has both `Enalopril`+`enalapril`, `Midoxidil`+`minoxidil`; cardio-ii both `Ranolazene`+`ranolazine`):
- `spec-los-thyroid-antithyroid-obesity-osteo-filled-4.json`, card `hypo`: has `liothyronone`, lacks **liothyronine**.
- `spec-gi-los-and-med-list-1.json`, card `5ht3`: has `dolasteron`, lacks **dolasetron**.
- `spec-antiplatelet-antithrombotics-fibrinolytics-med-list-los-3-12-26-1.json`, card `adp`: has `ticlopridine`, lacks **ticlopidine**.
- Rule: 90 §90.2.6 + the verbatim matching rule (a non-verbatim surface form fails silently, so the card won't attach to any table that spells the drug correctly).
- Correction: add the three correct spellings alongside her forms.
**F9 — NSAIDs/pain: "Symptomatic Management" is filed inside the DMT card.**

- File: `spec-med-list-nsaids-pain.json`; part `dmt @ b_2V23XY5P2P:563` runs to `:594`, swallowing the [U] heading at node 585 "Symptomatic Management" and its list (spasticity → baclofen/tizanidine; bladder → oxybutynin/tolterodine; sexual dysfun → sildenafil/tadalafil/alprostadil; fatigue → methylphenidate…). None of that is dz-modifying therapy, and the card title is her heading "dz-Modifying tx (DMTs)".
- Rule: convention 3 as applied throughout the draft (headed non-class sections get their own card — "Overflow Incontinence", "Non-Pharm", "Epilepsy" notes…).

- Correction: add a part at `b_2V23XY5P2P:585` — its own card (0 aliases, like Overflow Incontinence) or a further part of the `ms` card; not inside dmt. (The symptomatic drug names are correctly excluded from dmt's aliases — keep that.)
**F10 — NSAIDs/pain: the [U] "Acetaminophen" heading (node 328) closes the SMR card.**

- File: same spec; part `smr @ b_2V23XY5P2P:278` runs to `:329`, so the last unit of the skeletal-muscle-relaxants card is a stray underlined "Acetaminophen" line (heading-only, immediately before "Ergotamine alkaloids (class)" at 329, which is cut). It is a cross-reference to her Acetaminophen lecture at the file's top.
- Rule: conventions 1/4 (drug-name headings at class level are cut; one-line cross-refs stay with preceding content — but the preceding card here is unrelated).

- Correction (low severity): add a 1-unit part at `b_2V23XY5P2P:328` as a further part of the `apap` card (the further-part model already used for key-monitoring items), or its own card; it should not end the SMR card.
**F11 — cardio-1-1: underlined sub-class heading "Dihydropyridines:" not cut (consistency).**

- File: `spec-cardio-med-list-1-1.json`; card `ccb @ b_9812JX3SKW:296` spans 296–385 including the [U] ind0 heading at node 340 "Dihydropyridines:". The draft's own convention 1 cuts underlined sub-class headings (GI Phenothiazines/Butyrophenones/Benzamides; NSAID Salicylates/Acetic acid/Propionic/COX-2-i/Oxicams are separate cards). Same structural pattern, different treatment.
- Rule: convention 1 as stated and applied elsewhere; 90 §90.2.6.

- Correction (low severity): either cut at `:340` into a dihydropyridines card (aliases: amlodipine, clevidipine, felodipine, isradipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, nisoldipine) with ccb keeping the non-DHP part, or record the deliberate fold. The BB generation headings ([U] "Non-selective (1st Generation)" etc.) and vasodilator route headings ("Arterial: PVR") are sub-group labels like the benzo duration sub-groups — correctly not cut; only Dihydropyridines is a class name.
**F12 — aggregate, low: heading class names omitted from aliases.**

- Cards whose heading is a class name that is not in `aliases`, with no mis-attachment risk: GI `benzo` ("Benzodiazepines"), behavioral `adhdsnri` ("SNRI/non-stimulant"), `insatyp` ("Atypical antidepressant"), `instca` ("Tricyclic antidepressant"), GU `snri` ("Serotonin/Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor"), `b3bph` ("B3 agonist"), `estrogen` ("Topical/Vaginal Estrogens", "α1 adrenergic agonists"), NSAIDs `cgrpmab` ("Monoclonal Antibodies"). §90.2.6 lists "the class name as she wrote it" in aliases; the epilepsy-CCB precedent justifies omission only where it would mis-attach (see below). Correction: add them (or state the deliberate omission in the draft per the CCB precedent). Not urgent — impact is attachment via class mentions in condition text only.
## Flagged judgement points — explicit verdicts

- **Convention 3 (headed non-class sections become their own cards) — OK.** It is the right reading of §90.2.6's cut rule plus "nothing dropped/reordered": a headed section that is not a class gets its own card instead of being mislabeled into an unrelated drug card. The cardio-ii `hld` precedent is sound. It is applied inconsistently in three spots — F1, F9, F10 — which are the corrections.

- **Epilepsy "Calcium Channel Blockers" card with no class-name alias — OK (correct deliberate omission).** With the alias it would attach the epilepsy CCB card to cardiovascular CCB tables and condition text; without it the card still attaches via `ethosuximide`. This is exactly what convention 7's mis-attachment flag is for.

- **GU hematopoietic LO exception — OK.** The GU `lo` part ends where her "Med List: Hematopoietic Drugs" heading begins; the hematopoietic cards follow in order and the second LO part (`LOs Hematopoietic Drugs`, `@ b_7FHWZDE00H:176`) ends the file. Matches convention 5 and 20 §20.6 (lo = slice under its own heading).

- **Shared DTI/FXa key-monitoring item assigned to `dti` only — OK.** A part has one card; the item is kept exactly once, in order, and the DTI and FXa items that are per-class are split correctly (heparin card also carries the separate "LMWH and Fondaparinux" item).

- **Anesthetics `home: {}` — OK.** Per the design ruling (pharm/rules/sources): Anesthetics/sedation cards go to Surgery › Preoperative/Postoperative Care via `also`, plus any system whose tables contain those drugs. home.pance is not needed to guarantee appearance.
